brief: UBS's 2027-2028 outlook argues AI infrastructure build-out (hyperscaler capex rising from ~$1tr in 2026 to ~$1.75-1.8tr in 2027) has offset tariff and energy headwinds, driving over half of global trade growth and about 60% of US growth, so global growth accelerating from 3.2% to 3.5% in 2027 depends unusually on that capex continuing and on a Middle East resolution reviving Saudi/UAE oil volumes; public opposition to data centers, power and financing constraints are the main risk. US corporate profits sit at record highs (14.5% of GDP), concentrated in tech and financials, while earnings growth is expected to decelerate from 34.7% realized in 2026 to 17.8% in 2027 and 16.9% in 2028. UBS judges terminal rates mispriced too high, expects DM central banks to stay restrictive through 2027 before reversing hikes in 2028, and forecasts US 10-year yields near 4.80% by end-2027 on a bull-steepening curve. It sees no evidence of dedollarization but still prefers gold against EUR. Top trades include long Nasdaq vs Russell 2000, long V2X vs VIX, European 2s10s flatteners and long EU over US IG.
